title: Identifying Duplicate Code Smell
question: Which of the following statements best describes the 'Duplicate Code' smell?

options.text: A class performs only one action, delegating work to another class.
Understanding and maintaining a class costs time and money, but it doesn't do enough to earn your attention.
Two code fragments look almost identical.
A class contains only fields and crude methods for accessing them (getters and setters).

explanation: The 'Duplicate Code' smell occurs when two or more code fragments are very similar or identical. This is problematic because if a change is needed, it has to be made in all duplicated places, increasing the risk of errors and making maintenance harder.
